paraphrase: Call him Rāma or Rahīm, Kṛṣṇa or Mahādeva, Pārśvanātha or Brahmā — it is Brahman itself; as vessels differ but the clay is one, so the names differ while the self is one in nature.
notes: Pada widely ascribed to Ānandaghana; attribution and wording uncertain. The Jain reading is that every soul shares one nature, not that there is one soul.
